feed.title: Ted Tschopp's AI News
feed.subtitle: Latest AI News and Ratings from Ted Tschopp

entry.title: AI-Native Firms [ ! ]
entry.summary: This paper focuses on how AI-native companies are changing firm design by scaling revenue, output, and operating capacity with leaner teams and fewer traditional assets. The key takeaway is that agentic AI is not just improving productivity; it is lowering the minimum viable company threshold by replacing some fixed organizational layers with workflow orchestration, AI labor, and higher revenue-per-employee models.

entry.title: How agents are transforming work [ ! ]
entry.summary: This OpenAI piece explains how agentic AI is moving from chat-based assistance into delegated, long-horizon workflows where tools like Codex can execute meaningful work across engineering and knowledge-worker tasks. Our analysts emphasized that the managerial insight is the shift from idea engine to execution engine, with non-technical workers increasingly able to orchestrate AI agents, low-code workflows, and multimodal frontier models.

entry.title: Teach Your AI How You Make Decisions [ * ]
entry.summary: This HBR article argues that companies need to capture the tacit judgment of expert employees so AI agents can understand escalation thresholds, exception handling, risk signoff, and decision logic. Our analysts liked the mental model of building judgment infrastructure, but noted that the piece was light on implementation detail and should have engaged more deeply with knowledge engineering, protocol analysis, RAG, and knowledge graphs.

entry.title: Semantic Search for AI Agents at Scale: Retrieval and Ranking for LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant [ * ]
entry.summary: This LinkedIn Engineering article is a production case study in retrieval, ranking, semantic search, and evaluation for AI-powered recruiting at massive scale. Our analysts saw it as important because it shows how expert-judged labels, smaller execution models, ranking systems, and eval loops can turn a messy hiring marketplace into a more useful agentic search system.

entry.title: Ornith-1.0: Self-Scaffolding LLMs for Agentic Coding [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article covers a technical approach to agentic coding where LLMs create or adapt their own scaffolding to improve software-development workflows. The main value is as a signal of where coding agents are heading, but it remains more useful for technical readers tracking autonomous coding systems than for general AI leaders looking for immediately deployable operating guidance.

entry.title: Critique of Agent Model [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This paper critiques assumptions behind the agent model, including how autonomy, decision-making, and tool use are framed in current AI systems. The useful takeaway is conceptual discipline: leaders should avoid over-anthropomorphizing agents and should keep governance, evaluation, accountability, and human judgment at the center of agentic AI deployment.

entry.title: The AI Agents Stack [ ! ]
entry.summary: This article lays out a six-layer framework for moving from an LLM to a production-ready AI agent, including orchestration, memory, tools, evaluation, and guardrails. Our analysts rated it Essential because AI leaders urgently need a practical decision framework for agent architecture, especially as evaluation, control planes, and production guardrails remain underdeveloped.

entry.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents [ * ]
entry.summary: This article introduces Qwen's language-based world models for training general AI agents in simulated reinforcement learning environments across multiple task domains. Our analysts saw it as Important because it points to a cheaper, scalable path for agent training and benchmarking, while also reinforcing the strategic importance of open-weight model ecosystems globally.

entry.title: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil LLM-optimized inference chip [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article announces OpenAI's first custom inference-only chip, co-developed with Broadcom to improve LLM inference economics and reduce dependence on external AI hardware suppliers. Our analysts kept it Optional because the announcement lacked concrete benchmarks, availability, or performance metrics, making it more of a strategic signal about vertical integration and token pricing pressure than an actionable development today.

entry.title: How Loka Built a Natural, Low-Latency Voice Agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This AWS case study explains how Loka built a low-latency voice agent using Amazon Nova 2 Sonic and Bedrock, with attention to audio reasoning, pipeline design, and latency reduction. Our analysts rated it Optional because, while the technical walkthrough is useful, it felt promotional and did not demonstrate enough business value or differentiated performance beyond the AWS advertorial framing.

entry.title: The Problem is Prompt Debt [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article argues that organizations are accumulating "prompt debt" as prompts become embedded business logic across workflows, models, and one-off automations. Our analysts found the concept directionally useful for thinking about model lock-in and fragile prompt engineering, but rated it Optional because the piece was unevenly written and the problem may evolve quickly as agentic systems reduce direct prompt dependence.

entry.title: Thinking to recall: How reasoning unlocks parametric knowledge in LLMs [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This Google Research article explores how reasoning steps can help LLMs surface latent parametric knowledge that may not appear through direct recall alone. Our analysts treated it as Optional because the research is intellectually interesting for understanding reasoning, memory, and model behavior, but its immediate enterprise application is less clear than the more practical agent-stack and agent-training pieces.

entry.title: Introducing Claude Tag [ ! ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's announcement points to Claude becoming easier to invoke inside real workflows, moving the model closer to an embedded collaboration and task-execution layer. The key takeaway is that AI assistants are shifting from standalone chat tools toward agentic work interfaces where people can tag, delegate to, and coordinate with models as part of everyday knowledge work.

entry.title: LLMs Misunderstand Luxury Brands. Here's How to Optimize Your Marketing Strategy for AI [ ! ]
entry.summary: This article explains why LLMs often miss the implicit signals that luxury brands rely on, including scarcity, exclusivity, heritage, craftsmanship, and minimalist visual storytelling. The deeper insight is that marketers now have to optimize not only for human buyers but also for AI-mediated search and generative engine optimization, because LLMs are becoming curators that can reshape brand perception.

entry.title: From campaigns to continuous growth: AI capabilities shaping marketing [ * ]
entry.summary: McKinsey lays out how AI is changing marketing from episodic campaigns into continuous insight, scaled creativity, hyper-personalization, marketing to AI agents, and always-on full-funnel orchestration. Our analysts saw this as important because it captures the CMO shift toward 24/7 AI-driven growth systems, although they kept it below Essential because the article was more framework than action plan.

entry.title: Training a Legal Agent With Applied Compute [ * ]
entry.summary: Harvey's post describes how vertical AI companies can improve legal agents through applied compute, fine-tuning, evals, retrieval, tool orchestration, prompts, skills, and human review. The most useful insight is that even enterprises that do not fine-tune models still need the surrounding AI engineering discipline-better evals, better retrieval, workflow harnesses, and review loops-to encode proprietary business knowledge into reliable agentic systems.

entry.title: Alibaba's AI video model rises to No. 2 in global rankings, as OpenAI's Sora and ByteDance's Seedance fall away [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article covers Alibaba's Happy Horse text-to-video and image-to-video model moving up global AI video rankings while Sora and Seedance lose ground. Our analysts treated it as optional because benchmark movement in generative video is volatile, use-case fit remains unclear, and the broader story is more about rapid Chinese model competition than immediate enterprise actionability.

entry.title: Building pay-per-intelligence for AI agents: How Ampersend uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This AWS post explains how Ampersend uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments and payment protocols to let autonomous AI agents pay for data, APIs, models, or content during a workflow. The takeaway is that agent payments and pay-per-intelligence infrastructure will matter as autonomous agents transact across services, but the analysts viewed this specific article as more vendor implementation note than must-read strategy.

entry.title: Building an AI Database for Agentic GTM Operations [ ! ]
entry.summary: This article lays out how Rippling/Databricks-style data architecture can support agentic GTM and sales operations by reorganizing customer and workflow data for AI agents. Our analysts rated it Essential because go-to-market is one of the highest-impact enterprise AI use cases, and the key lesson is that agentic sales workflows require a strong data foundation, not just a chatbot or prompt layer.

entry.title: Daybreak: Tools for securing every organization in the world [ ! ]
entry.summary: OpenAI's Daybreak announcement focuses on using advanced AI systems to strengthen cybersecurity tooling and help organizations defend themselves at scale. Our analysts treated it as Essential because AI security is becoming a core enterprise requirement, and OpenAI's move signals that frontier-model providers are increasingly competing to own the cybersecurity control plane.

entry.title: Sakana Fugu [ * ]
entry.summary: Sakana Fugu introduces a multimodal orchestration model that routes user requests across multiple LLMs and combines outputs to improve answer quality. Our analysts saw it as Important because model routing, LLM councils, inference engineering, and orchestration layers are emerging as a major architecture trend, even though latency, token cost, and transparency remain concerns.

entry.title: The seven operating truths of AI-native companies [ ~ ]
entry.summary: McKinsey's article describes operating principles for AI-native companies, including differentiation, security, and treating AI agents as capabilities rather than simple tools. Our analysts rated it Optional because the guidance felt conventional and somewhat behind the agentic future, with less practical implementation detail than AI leaders need.

entry.title: Freeing the Law with LOCUS: A Local Ordinance Corpus for the United States [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This research paper introduces LOCUS, a corpus designed to make local U.S. ordinances more accessible and usable for AI systems, legal research, and civic applications. Our analysts viewed it as a valuable public-good dataset, but Optional for AI leaders because its immediate relevance is strongest for legal-tech, civic-tech, and public-sector use cases.

entry.title: Teaching Sidekick to say no: automated data curation with LLM judge consensus [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Shopify explains how it curated refusal data and used LLM judge consensus to train Sidekick to say no when appropriate, reducing hallucination and sycophancy risks. Our analysts rated it Optional because the case study is useful for guardrails, refusals, and evaluation workflows, but the pattern is something mature AI teams should already be implementing.

entry.title: Agentic coding and persistent returns to expertise [ ! ]
entry.summary: This Anthropic research analyzes Claude Code usage to show how agentic coding shifts humans toward planning while AI systems handle more execution decisions. Our analysts rated it Essential because the data reinforces that domain expertise, task decomposition, and management-style instruction remain critical to productivity gains from AI coding agents.

entry.title: Building DoorDash Assistant: An engineering overview [ ! ]
entry.summary: This DoorDash engineering overview explains how the company built an AI assistant using personalization, AI memory, and task-oriented workflows to support consumer decisions such as grocery selection under budget and dietary constraints. Our analysts saw it as Essential because it is a concrete production example of agentic AI moving beyond chatbot interaction into context-aware, personalized action inside a real consumer platform.

entry.title: MosaicLeaks: Can your research agent keep a secret? [ * ]
entry.summary: This ServiceNow research introduces MosaicLeaks, a benchmark for privacy leakage in deep research agents, including intent leakage, answer leakage, and full information leakage. Our analysts rated it Important because deep research agents are becoming a core enterprise LLM use case, and leaders need to understand how private information can leak even when users are not deliberately sharing sensitive data.

entry.title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action [ * ]
entry.summary: This McKinsey piece examines how agentic AI could reshape advertising from attention capture toward delegated consumer action, with scenarios involving closed webs, autonomous delegation, and curated ecosystems. Our analysts landed on Important because the article gives marketers useful categories and data, even though they debated how much AI agents will truly centralize consumer decision-making versus subtly shaping the context around decisions.

entry.title: The Strongest Teams of AI Agents Will be Built Using Different Models [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This HBR article argues that stronger AI agent teams will come from using diverse models, data sources, personalities, and governance approaches. Our analysts rated it Optional because the core idea of model diversity is sound, but they found the piece thinly researched, light on empiricism, and less useful than practical guidance on governed enterprise data, workflow design, and model portfolio management.

entry.title: Human Capital, AI, and Labor Commoditization [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This research paper studies how the arrival of ChatGPT affected labor-market pricing on Upwork, finding that price became more important while credentials, reputation, and self-presentation declined in relative weight. Our analysts rated it Optional because the commoditization effect in task-based online labor markets felt unsurprising and only incrementally useful for AI leaders deciding what to do next.

entry.title: Project Fetch: Phase two [ ! ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's Project Fetch shows Claude Opus 4.7 controlling a robot dog in a physical environment, with newer general-purpose model capabilities automating far more robotics tasks without specialized robotics optimization. Our analysts rated it Essential because the real takeaway is strategic: general-purpose AI models are improving in unexpected domains, creating uncertainty about where future competition, automation, and agentic capability will emerge.

entry.title: Anthropic ships major Claude Design overhaul with design system imports, code round-trips, and a fix for its token-burning problem [ ! ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Design update improves enterprise design workflows by connecting brand systems, design tools, code round-trips, and token-efficiency changes into a more usable AI work platform. Our analysts saw this as Essential because Claude is moving toward an ERP of intelligence, potentially giving non-technical teams a unified AI stack for presentations, spreadsheets, research, sales, marketing, and brand-consistent work.

entry.title: The symbiotic enterprise [ * ]
entry.summary: McKinsey's report argues that enterprises must transform into hybrid, agentic organizations where humans provide judgment, creativity, governance, and exception handling while AI agents and robots handle much of the operational work. Our analysts rated it Important because it frames AI transformation around organizational capability and proprietary intelligence, though they criticized it for being high-level, sales-oriented, and too traditional in how it draws boundaries between humans and agents.

entry.title: How OpenAI Built Its Data Agent [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article explains OpenAI's data-agent architecture, including offline data preparation, runtime flow, tool use, and the importance of bringing the right tables and representations into the reasoning process. Our analysts rated it Optional because it is technically interesting but limited for most AI leaders, with the main takeaway being that simple, well-structured systems often outperform more complex agentic architectures.

entry.title: Self-improving Memory for Agents [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Perplexity's announcement describes an agent memory system that recursively improves itself by reorganizing context, semantic information, and memory structures between sessions. Our analysts rated it Optional because it is still a product announcement, but the deeper insight is that agentic systems may increasingly require background sleep-like processes to improve retrieval, reasoning, and long-term performance.

entry.title: How Preply combines AI and human tutors to personalize learning [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Preply is using OpenAI's API to transcribe tutoring sessions, analyze recordings, and provide personalized feedback to language learners and human tutors. Our analysts rated it Optional because the adoption metrics are interesting, but the article offers limited technical detail on how the learning insights or self-learning exercise engine actually work.

entry.title: Financial Services Agents in Production [ ! ]
entry.summary: This LangChain report examines how major financial services firms, such as J.P. Morgan, are putting AI agents into production across real enterprise workflows. Our analysts highlighted its concrete examples, production lessons, and transferable recipes for organizations looking to operationalize Generative AI beyond pilots.

entry.title: The Evolution of Agentic Surfaces: Building with Claude Managed Agents [ ! ]
entry.summary: Anthropic lays out Claude Managed Agents and explains how production AI agents require more than prompts, including sessions, environments, secrets, observability, and scalable agent harnesses. Our analysts emphasized this as a practical primer for AI leaders building agentic AI systems, especially because it explains the infrastructure needed to move from prototypes to production.

entry.title: Don't Let AI Slop Muck Up Your Company's Processes [ * ]
entry.summary: This article warns that low-quality AI output can degrade organizational processes, knowledge, and accountability over time. Our analysts focused on the risk of de-skilling, the need for strong evals, and why leaders must actively manage AI automation rather than assuming AI will fix broken workflows.

entry.title: BBVA Puts AI At the Core of Banking with OpenAI [ * ]
entry.summary: BBVA's case study shows how a major bank scaled ChatGPT and OpenAI tools from early adoption to broad enterprise deployment. Our analysts noted useful lessons around executive training, governance, AI champions, and top-down adoption, while also flagging vendor lock-in and limited transferability as concerns.

entry.title: Building Supercharger: How Rocket Close optimized title operations with agentic AI [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Rocket Close's Supercharger project applies agentic AI to improve title operations and support human agents in a real estate workflow. Our analysts found the architecture and reported efficiency gains useful, but viewed the case study as relatively thin and less actionable than stronger enterprise AI examples.

entry.title: Why Weibo's tiny VibeThinker-3B has the AI world arguing over benchmarks again [ ~ ]
entry.summary: VibeThinker-3B is a small AI reasoning model claiming strong math and coding benchmark performance through specialized reinforcement learning and a spectrum-to-signal training approach. Our analysts found the small-model innovation interesting, but treated the article as optional because benchmark results may not translate to real-world AI performance.

entry.title: Factory 2.0: From coding agents to software factories [ ! ]
entry.summary: Factory's post frames the next step in AI software development as a full software factory, where coding agents, model routing, model independence, and automated engineering workflows operate more like an assembly line than a single developer tool. The key analyst insight is that recursive self-improvement, continual learning, and lights-out software production could become essential strategic questions for AI leaders, even if human oversight and real case studies still matter.

entry.title: Qwen-Robot Suite: A Foundation Model Suite for Physical World Intelligence [ * ]
entry.summary: Qwen-Robot Suite introduces an open foundation model stack for embodied AI, including navigation, world modeling, and manipulation models for physical-world robotics. Our analysts saw this as an important signal because Qwen's open-source LLM momentum could translate into physical AI and robotics, although near-term enterprise adoption remains limited for most AI leaders.

entry.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks [ * ]
entry.summary: Z.ai's GLM-5.2 is an open-weight model aimed at long-horizon agentic workflows, coding, software engineering, and million-token context use cases. Our analysts rated it important because Chinese open models such as GLM-5.2 are getting close enough to proprietary frontier models to replace a meaningful share of enterprise workflows, with sparse attention and compute efficiency adding to the strategic relevance.

entry.title: Introducing SubQ 1.1 Small [ ~ ]
entry.summary: SubQ 1.1 Small presents a sub-quadratic language model architecture designed to scale more efficiently than traditional transformer attention, particularly for long-context and needle in a haystack retrieval-style tasks. Our analysts found the architecture interesting but optional because the claims are still mostly vendor-led and there are not yet meaningful enterprise case studies or implementation examples.

entry.title: Pretrained to Imagine, Fine-Tuned to Act: The Rise of World-Action Models [ ~ ]
entry.summary: NVIDIA's post explains world-action models, showing how video world models can be adapted into action models for robotics and embodied AI systems. Our analysts viewed it as a useful primer on world models, robot action planning, and NVIDIA's physical AI stack, but optional for most AI leaders because robotics is still not a near-term priority for many enterprises.

entry.title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World [ ~ ]
entry.summary: ENPIRE explores agentic robot policy self-improvement, using recursive loops and coding models to help robotic systems learn and refine real-world skills. Our analysts saw the research as fascinating for autonomous action, guardrails, and recursive self-improvement, but optional because only organizations already working directly on robotics are likely to need this level of technical detail now.

entry.title: How Gen AI is Disrupting B2B Buying Decisions [ * ]
entry.summary: Generative AI is reshaping B2B purchasing by moving product discovery, evaluation, and recommendations into AI-mediated environments where buyers increasingly rely on large language models and answer engines rather than traditional search and vendor-controlled channels. Our analysts highlighted the growing shift from SEO to GEO/AEO (Generative Engine Optimization and Answer Engine Optimization), making it essential for organizations to rethink how their content, expertise, and brand are surfaced by AI systems that increasingly influence buying decisions.

entry.title: Sakana AI Launches Its First Commercial Product, Sakana Marlin [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Sakana AI has launched its first commercial product, Sakana Marlin, an autonomous AI research assistant designed to perform weeks of strategy analysis in hours by acting as a virtual Chief Strategy Officer. Our analysts viewed this as an early example of a broader trend toward profession-specific AI agents that conduct long-horizon research and produce executive-ready reports, but considered it too early in its commercialization cycle to have immediate strategic implications for most AI leaders.
